mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen every week for four weeks (-39.6 to -30.4), the largest cumulative improvement of any series. A continued monotonic rise in WORKPLACES rebuilds commuting and lunchtime routines that generate weekday footfall in retail corridors, so mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days (-46.05).
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improves from -39.6 at t-3w to -30.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is less than or equal to -46.05 while WORKPLACES continues to rise or holds at or above -30.4.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has sat in a narrow band (-71.9 to -68.1) for four weeks. A first crossing above -70 marks the point where enough discretionary transit trips resume to feed non-essential retail catchments, so RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks of the crossing rather than staying near -46.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -70 for the first time after at least three consecutive weeks at or below -70
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT values -71.3, -71.9, -70.0, -68.1 across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses above -70 and the following 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC does not exceed the 14-day mean ending at t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has normalised fastest (-16.4 to -10.0), meaning stock-up and pharmacy-only trip behaviour is fading, while TRANSIT is simultaneously recovering. The joint signal indicates households switching from essential-only errands to mixed-purpose trips, and the retail component of those trips lifts RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM within 12 points of baseline while TRANSIT improves at least 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moves -16.4 to -10.0 while TRANSIT moves -71.9 to -68.1
failure_condition: When both GROCERY_PHARM is within 12 points of baseline and TRANSIT improves at least 2 points week-on-week, the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean is below the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Melbourne's staged easing path removes the stay-at-home direction that suppressed retail. Conditional on an announced easing step, the released restriction mechanically reopens non-essential retail premises, so RETAIL_REC moves toward baseline over the following four weeks, with WORKPLACES confirming the reopening is real rather than a reporting artefact.
candidate_trigger: public announcement of a restrictions-easing step that reopens non-essential retail
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC already improving -47.7 to -43.7 and WORKPLACES -39.6 to -30.4
regime_hint: restrictions easing toward reopening, not tightening
failure_condition: Following an announced easing step, the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean stays at or below the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL remains 16.6 points above baseline, so a large share of the population is still home-anchored. The recent RETAIL_REC gain (-47.7 to -43.7) is the low-hanging rebound from essential trips; without a further fall in RESIDENTIAL the discretionary component stalls, leaving the next 28-day mean below the last 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays at or above +15 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL only eases from 19.3 to 16.6 across four weeks
regime_hint: partial reopening with residual stay-at-home behaviour
failure_condition: With RESIDENTIAL at or above +15 for two consecutive weeks, the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the last-28-day mean by more than 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is the most normalised series (-10.0) and has improved in each of the last four weeks, making it a leading indicator of household out-of-home trip frequency. Its continued weekly improvement propagates into broader retail trips within one week, lifting RETAIL_REC immediately rather than over a full month.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM improves again in the next week while the following 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the 7-day mean ending at t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES (-39.6 to -30.4) and TRANSIT (-71.9 to -68.1) are improving together, which means trips are being generated by both work and non-work motives rather than one substituting for the other. Joint improvement signals broad re-mobility, so retail catchments widen and RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improve in the t-2w to t-0w window
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve in the same week, the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS rebounds from -28.1 to -17.1 as spring weather arrives alongside eased outdoor rules. Outdoor recreation absorbs discretionary time and spending that would otherwise go to indoor retail, so a PARKS reading above -20 predicts a weaker RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumps from -28.1 at t-1w to -17.1 at t-0w
regime_hint: spring weather transition with outdoor activity permitted
failure_condition: PARKS is above -20 and the following 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the 14-day mean ending at t-0w.
